_meta.status: DRAFT — not tuned and not ready to import. It carries the rooms design that was cut from Chapter 2 so it is not lost. Numbers are placeholders scaled off Ch2's; the shape is the part worth reviewing.
_meta.theChapterInOneLine: Chapter 2 gave you a calendar of gigs that would take anyone. This chapter gives you venues with opinions: rooms that want a kind of song, and crowds that tire of hearing it.
newInThisChapter: ROOMS — the stage group grows from one bar to several. Each room is a bar you tap to play, with its own size, payout and fatigue.

GENRE — songs gain tags and rooms gain taste. A room drinks ONE genre of setlist currency, so which songs you learn decides which rooms you can work. This is why Ch2's songs deliberately had no tags: there was nothing to match against.

FAN FATIGUE debuts here: each room carries a perFill factor below 1 scaled by its own fillCount, so the same room pays less every time you work it. Rotation is the answer, and this is the chapter that has rooms to rotate.

maxActive rises 1 → 2 → 3. Working several rooms at once is the chapter's arc and the mechanical meaning of 'a local circuit'. (Needs a setMaxActive payload; Ch2 sidestepped this by setting maxActive to the bar count.)
MERCH — a second income stream (provisional placement; it could equally sit in Ch4 with touring).
_meta.continuityFromCh2: Chapter 2 is a gig-cycle economy (timed bars, standing bookings, Buzz). This chapter keeps the bar-as-gig shape but the bars are now ROOMS with genre taste, and FAN FATIGUE debuts here — the same crowd tires of you, so rotating rooms is the play. Do not assume fatigue was taught earlier; it was not.
openQuestions: Does merch belong here or in Ch4? Here it is a second income stream in a chapter that already has rooms, genre and automation. Ch4 (touring) may need it more.
Three genres or four? Three keeps the song list short; four makes room taste more distinctive.
Should the booking agent automate the ROOM (fills on its own) or the TAP (fires the set for you)? The second is closer to Ch1's automation feel; the first is closer to an actual agent.

chapter.name: Local Venues
chapter.theme: The club on Third, the record store's back room, the legion hall. Places that book bands, each with its own crowd and its own idea of a good night.
chapter.storyBeatOpenDraft: Turns out there are four stages in this town that will book a band, and every one of them wants something slightly different. You have a van, a set, and a phone number for a woman who books Thursdays.

roomPayoutRecordBuff.note: The chapter's prestige lever: Records raise what winning a room pays, never how fast a room fills (§11). Chapter 2 gets the same effect from the root Records modifier on Cash, since its payouts are Cash yields; rooms here pay Fans, so a chapter-local buff is needed and is deliberately NOT on the fan rate.

constants.fatigueNote: 0.85 per win. Fatigue is introduced in THIS chapter, with rotation available from the start as its answer. With three rooms the player routes around it rather than hitting a wall.

currencies.note: One setlist currency per genre. A room names one as its fillCurrency — a direct reference, never an intersected target. This is how room taste is expressed without a preference table.

producers.note: Fired by a room's `tap`. Pays every genre the player has songs for; each room drinks only its own, so a set you cannot play pays nothing into a room that wants it.

groups.name: The Song List
groups.note: As Ch2, but songs now carry a genre tag and their reward multiplies that genre's line. The first song of a genre sets that genre's flag and opens its line.

groups.name: The Circuit
groups.maxActiveNote: The chapter's arc. One room is a residency; three is a circuit. §12.7: raising maxActive is an unlock, not a multiplier. `setMaxActive` as an upgrade payload does not exist in code yet.

bars.name: The Legion Hall
bars.note: A big room of a genre the player already has. Two loud rooms is deliberate — it tests whether genre or room size drives the choice.

upgradesDraft.name: The Booking Agent
upgradesDraft.note: The chapter's idle step. See openQuestions on whether the agent fills rooms or fires the set.

capstoneDraft.name: Headline the Ballroom
capstoneDraft.note: The regional 'big' private venue — the room everyone in town plays once they matter.

importerExtensionsNeeded: grantCurrency as a reward type (shared with Ch2)
tags on a reward, so fatigue targets the payouts as a set (shared with Ch2)
setMaxActive as an upgrade payload — §12.7 sanctions the concept, no code yet
